# k8sight

> k8sight is a free, open-source native desktop app (macOS, Windows and Linux) for browsing and operating any Kubernetes cluster from your local kubeconfig. It gives you a live dashboard, pod logs, an in-pod shell, interactive topology, Helm, Argo CD, Flux CD and Flagger, a built-in Security Center (image CVEs, config and RBAC audit via bundled Trivy), a bring-your-own-model AI assistant, and one-click AWS EKS / Azure AKS onboarding, with nothing to install in-cluster. A demo mode lets you try every feature with no cluster required.

## What k8sight is

- **Category:** a desktop UI for Kubernetes clusters you already have: a peer of Lens and k9s, not a management platform like Rancher.
- **Runs where:** on your laptop. It reads your kubeconfig and operates no servers of its own; the local API binds to 127.0.0.1 by default.
- **Price:** free and open-source (MIT-style license). No account or sign-in required.
- **Platforms:** macOS (Apple Silicon .dmg), Windows (x64 .exe), Linux (.AppImage and .deb), plus a Docker image.
- **Requirements:** kubectl on your PATH and a working kubeconfig. It does not require the aws, az, kubelogin or helm CLIs.

## How k8sight compares

- **vs Rancher:** Rancher is a multi-cluster platform you deploy inside clusters to provision and govern a fleet for a team. k8sight is a local desktop app that reads your kubeconfig and needs nothing in-cluster. Rancher's AI assistant (Liz) and MCP server come with a Rancher Prime subscription. Use Rancher to govern a fleet; use k8sight as a fast local cockpit for clusters you already run.
- **vs Lens:** the same category (a desktop UI). Lens requires a Lens ID sign-in and has its own AI assistant (Lens Prism), an MCP server (since March 2026), Flux views and AWS/Azure cloud integrations. k8sight needs no account, its AI assistant and MCP server work with any OpenAI-compatible model, and it adds a built-in security scanner (bundled Trivy), cost views, Argo CD, Flux and Flagger views, GKE onboarding and a no-cluster demo mode.
- **vs k9s:** k9s is a free, open-source terminal UI with no built-in AI or MCP server. k8sight is a graphical app with the AI assistant, MCP server, security scanning, costs, GitOps views and cloud onboarding listed above.
- **AI and MCP at a glance:** k8sight, Lens and Rancher Prime all have an AI assistant and an MCP server; only k8sight needs no account or subscription. k8sight works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; Rancher's Liz supports Ollama, OpenAI, Gemini and AWS Bedrock. Details are from public docs as of October 2026.

## Key features

- Live cluster dashboard: node and pod health, workload charts, capacity.
- Every workload type with live CPU/memory and cross-links (namespace → node → pod → owner).
- Pod logs, an in-pod shell (real TTY), and port-forwarding.
- Interactive pan/zoom topology graph and lazy-loaded Custom Resource tree.
- Helm releases with values and rendered manifests.
- First-class Argo CD GitOps dashboard with sync/refresh/rollback.
- Flux CD dashboard: Kustomizations, HelmReleases and sources with reconcile, suspend and resume; Flagger canary, A/B and blue/green rollout tracking.
- Security Center: image CVEs, config and RBAC audit, exposed secrets, via Trivy Operator reports or a bundled Trivy binary.
- One-click AWS EKS and Azure AKS onboarding across accounts/subscriptions; GKE, on-prem, kind and minikube work from your existing kubeconfig.
- Bring-your-own-model AI assistant grounded in live cluster data (secrets redacted before anything leaves the app).
- MCP server so external AI agents can inspect the cluster, including costs, Security Center findings, Argo CD, Flux and Flagger (read tools by default; write tools such as sync, reconcile and canary restart are opt-in).
- Demo mode: a realistic synthetic cluster, no kubeconfig required.
